summary: I noncaused extinction contrasts with III causative extinguishing and III Detransitive inability-to-be-extinguished (1/9). A perceived result or English/German intransitive paraphrase does not change the stem.
I.1 inherits both erlöschen and anstecken (Krankheit). The corpus batch contains no infection event to justify revising that inherited wording or numbering. Cooling water is added as I.2.
The qaṭəl-plus-ko forms at 69/309–310 and 96/79 contrast with Infectum ṭofe and plural ṭafən. Correct the existing box before calling ko-Preterit wholly unattested.
The extinguished lamp in Talay 2/26 becomes an omen in the narrative; the verb still denotes literal extinction, not a new divination sense.
Round 1 already supplies active III Infectum examples, so the repeated reader new_form claims for that box are wrong. New -wa boxes this round are I Infectum-wa and III Infectum-wa.

The kiln exchange /725–730 contains a correction of causal agency: workers close and leave the kiln, but direct extinguishing is denied. Preserve both the earlier proposal and the explicit repair in analysis.
Reduced ṭəfyo/ṭəfyowa spellings are retained. gəd- and k- contexts favor Infectum forms; they must not be collapsed with qaṭəl ṭafyo ko-Preterit already distinguished in round 1.
No new support for cooling water I.2 or infection is supplied. Water as extinguisher in the analogy is not the heated-water subject of round-1 I.2.
Is water cooling with ṭfy conventional, or a metonymic reference to loss of heat? The bath context supports the published broad gloss, based on one attestation.
What heat source and reference of taḥta/taḥtayye are intended in the recipes? Turoyo omits the object; retain the edition’s own hotplate parenthesis.
Reconcile PrS 38/62 with inherited prs 103/18,19 via the edition text/page mapping; identical wording alone does not authorise replacing one reference.
At 2.5/1232 what feminine referent has gone out? A recording comment is possible; no example is selected.
Confirm whether businesses ṭafən is conventional outside 1.16/604; the new figurative I.3 currently rests on one clear attestation.
Turning off cooking heat preserves löschen with an omitted heat/flame object; the German hotplate is supplied editorially and does not establish a new appliance sense.
The fire goes out mə qəm ruḥa, without a causative participant; this supports the inherited I versus III valency contrast, not a Detransitive relabelling.

The water/fire opposition depicts opposing parties; the creator of šar is responsible for ending it. Literal fire vocabulary in /5556 is retained under III.1, while /5559 has the opposing side as figurative patient.
